subject: Post-demo recap: Medisure data handling tradeoffs & proposed pilot
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@medisure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: Medisure data handling tradeoffs & proposed pilot

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo chat this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum.

Recap of Medisure requirements we captured (please correct anything I missed):
- Priority A: No persistent storage of PHI-sensitive prompt/response payloads (you called this "0-retention for PII").
- Priority B: Data residency in the US (primary: us-east region).
- Priority C: Short-lived telemetry/logs for debugging must not contain full PII; ideally hashed or sampled.
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, encryption-at-rest keys (KMS), and an operations MOP you can review.

What we proposed on the call (high level):
- Ephemeral mode: request-level inputs can be configured not to be written to long-term storage.
- Short-term logs / sampled traces for debugging (configurable retention window).
- Residency pinning to us-east; key management integrations are supported.

Suggested pilot (so Legal/Eng can evaluate):
1) Pilot length: 30 days internal evaluation + 30 days joint testing.
2) Mode: Ephemeral mode for full request/response text (no persistence).
3) Operational logs: hashed transaction indices + sampled traces retained for 7 days; full-text only on explicit, auditable upload by Medisure.
4) Evidence pack: SOC 2 summary + redwood-data-policies.pdf (attached).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm that pilot framing is acceptable to Medisure procurement/legal.
- If yes, we share the MOP (attached: medisure-proposed-mop-v1.docx) and a brief mutual action plan.
- Connect legal teams: please introduce Benjamin Ross (or let me know who on your side will be the legal reviewer).

Attachments: redwood-data-policies.pdf, medisure-proposed-mop-v1.docx

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up with Ben if that moves things faster.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
<aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Redwood Inference — inference that scales

From: Sara Li <sara.li@medisure.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Benjamin Ross <ben.ross@medisure.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Medisure data handling tradeoffs & proposed pilot

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear summary. This is very close to what we need. A few clarifications and asks from procurement/legal before we can greenlight a pilot: 

1) When you say "ephemeral mode for full request/response text (no persistence)" — we need to validate that nothing that could be used to re-identify PHI is stored in plaintext anywhere in your systems (including any debug dumps or temporary caches). Is that guaranteed in pilot mode?

2) If you require any troubleshooting captures, we prefer those to be collected only after explicit on-demand approval from our security team, and then transferred via secure upload.

3) Telemetry/logs: 7-day hashed indices sounds reasonable, but legal will want to see an example of the hashed format and proof we can't reverse it.

4) Please include SOC 2 summary (Type II) and KMS key flow diagrams in your evidence pack.

5) Please attach your proposed MOP and highlight any operational steps that create longer-lived artifacts. I attached a short redlines doc with a few CYA items for your review (medisure-redlines.pdf).

If you can get us the evidence pack + a tuned MOP we can loop in procurement and Ben this week. We are targeting a limited pilot with a small set of internal clinicians and test data by mid-November.

Sara
Sara Li
Director, Platform Security | Medisure Inc
sara.li@medisure.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 07:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap: Medisure data handling tradeoffs & proposed pilot

Aisha / Neha — quick technical note to feed back into Aisha's pilot framing before we send to Medisure.

Summary: Redwood supports an "ephemeral pipeline" where full prompt+response blobs are never written to long-term object storage. However, a few practical constraints and options to call out explicitly: 

- KV cache and streaming: when a request is served from GPU with streaming enabled, there are ephemeral in-memory buffers and rolling logs for metrics. These buffers are not persisted by default but debugging mode can snapshot them — snapshots are persisted if debugging mode is turned on.

- Debug snapshots: we can implement an "on-request snapshot" flow that only persists when Medisure requests it (secure upload), which satisfies the "explicit on-demand approval" ask. We'll need an API + audit event to capture who authorized the snapshot.

- Log sampling: instead of retaining every transaction index for 7 days, propose we store HMACed transaction IDs + a 0.5% sampled trace store (full trace redacted) for 7 days. Sampled traces have PII redacted by default; we can also provide a cryptographic hash-only representation for legal review to show non-reversibility.

- SOC2 / KMS: we can include the standard Type II summary and a KMS diagram. For the pilot we can offer Medisure a dedicated KMS customer key (bring-your-own-key) scoped to the pilot.

Proposed tweak to pilot to reduce risk and accelerate signoff:
1) Pilot mode: Ephemeral for full-text (no persistence) + hashed transaction indices retained 7 days.
2) Sampling: 0.5% sampled traces (redacted) retained 7 days; additional full-text snapshots only via explicit Medisure request and secure upload.
3) Residency: pin to us-east and restrict operations admin access to US-based personnel for the pilot window.

I'll attach the internal ops playbook excerpt that maps how snapshots are gated (ephemeral-ops-playbook.pdf). If legal wants to validate the hash format, we can produce a short reproducible example strip (no customer data) to demonstrate non-reversibility.

If that sounds good, Aisha — I recommend we send Medisure the tuned MOP and the example hash artifact.

-Vivek
Director, Inference Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@medisure.com>, Benjamin Ross <ben.ross@medisure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Medisure data handling tradeoffs & proposed pilot

Sara / Ben — thanks for the redlines, Ben if you'd prefer a short call I'm happy to set it up. Per Vivek's notes above, attached is a tuned MOP and the ops playbook excerpt. Highlights for legal review: 

- Pilot framing we will send: Ephemeral full-text (no persistence) + HMACed transaction indices retained 7 days + 0.5% sampled redacted traces retained 7 days.
- Debug snapshots: only created after Medisure approval via an auth workflow; snapshots uploaded to Medisure-controlled storage.
- Residency: pinned to us-east for the pilot; RBAC limited to US-based ops.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II summary included in the evidence pack; KMS BYOK option available.

Requested next steps: 
1) Medisure to confirm acceptance of the pilot framing above or propose changes (highlight in the attached medisure-proposed-mop-v1.docx).
2) Ben/Legal to confirm required wording and whether a short NDA amendment is needed.
3) If accepted, we'll create a one-page mutual action plan and a DocuSign packet (link below) to formalize the pilot window.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/packets/MS-2026-014-MOP
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/medisure

Attachments: medisure-proposed-mop-v1.docx, redwood-data-policies.pdf, ephemeral-ops-playbook.pdf

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute legal+security alignment this week? I can propose times.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com
